rationale: Both validate the diagram format thoroughly, sort a copy of the children and map plant codes cleanly. A computes each child's plants once in NewGarden and stores them in a simple map, which makes Plants a trivial lookup. It also checks that the diagram has enough cups for all the children. B defers the work to Plants via an index map, keeps an unused children field in the struct, and never checks whether the rows are long enough for the number of children. A garden with more children than cup pairs would therefore make B panic with an out-of-range index rather than return an error. B's error messages are slightly more descriptive, but A's simpler state and the missing robustness check in B favour A.
